notes:
The den is the old gatehouse-office of Unit 7, a brick outbuilding on the street corner of a warehouse lot at the end of a cul-de-sac service road; the road runs along the +z side, 8 m tiles at z 10..18, T-ing into a side road at x -36 and dead-ending at x 47.
Behind the den the warehouse (z -17) and its wing (x -17) stay where they are; the lot's driveway now comes in from the street at x 10..14 through a boom gate, up the +x side past three bays and a van, and onto the loading apron, which is why the truck lane, bay stripes and lit bay exist.
West of the den a chain-link compound (x -17..-9.5, z -13..9.7) holds the warehouse's containers, skip, drums and scrap, walled by the wing, open to the apron at its north end, with a locked double gate onto the street and its own crossover; the den keeps a 3.25 m strip of its own junk between its windows and that fence.
Across the street a small joinery (Unit A, sawtooth roof, roller doors turned to face +x so the camera sees them) sits at the frame's left edge with a lorry in its forecourt, a second metal unit further west, and a vacant lot with weeds and a hoarding to the east; a bench and bus flag stand on the far footpath.
Lighting tells the story at night: sodium columns on the far kerb every 16 m, cold LED posts on the lot, the warm bay and door, the amber beacon, with the power poles kept to the near side west of the den so no pole ever crosses the room on screen; 16 outdoor lights in all (10 today).
